title: Negative: with the finite-range penalty clipped to oversized bodies (no hidden growth drive), 7 settings of shedding, uptake and regrowth give boom-bust, extinction or a merged sea, never sustained crawling division
summary: Follow-up to 20261025T0908-c04-crawler-divide-confound, world.py of that contribution with bV=1, okclip=1, seed 1, t=600. shed 0.1: grows to 11 bodies then extinct. shed 0.2: 2-3 crawlers (16 body lengths) but max generation 2. kup 0.06, shed 0.1: the founder's progeny fill the domain, food runs out, starving cells die and 3 round static cells remain (genuine starvation deaths, ocsk/sheet.png). kup 0.05 with shed 0.15/0.25 and regrowth rn 0.003/0.006: extinction after a boom to 26 (0.15/0.003), one domain-filling body (0.15/0.006, occupancy 1.0), or few bodies with merge/split 0.53-0.75 and no persistent splits (0.25). The crawl-and-divide regime of the claim does not survive removing the content-independent growth drive at these settings; the initial food stock (n0=1 everywhere) drives a boom that the slow regrowth cannot sustain. Not tried: starting food at the regrowth-limited level, or a smaller cost of motion with a larger kernel.

finding.result: no setting gives max generation >= 3 with persistent crawlers; boom-bust, extinction or merged sea
